scope: read-only review; all repro writes were confined to disposable temporary directories; no network registry calls

findings.impact: The public INN-list tool unexpectedly enables local CSV file reads and writes outside its declared save/evidence arguments, and bypasses its 50-ID cap. Existing non-result files are appended to. No shell execution or remote unauthenticated exploit was established. This is not the documented snapshot-cache feature: flags and destination path are smuggled in inns.
findings.fix: Validate each item as an INN before constructing argv; explicitly reject paths and option-like input, or send validated IDs through --stdin. If preserving invalid-ID rows, reject non-ID strings without invoking CLI parsing. Add no-write/no-path-expansion regression tests.

findings.trigger: counterparty_verdict with INN_CHECK_MCP_TIMEOUT=0.15 and an offline test engine sleeping 0.8 seconds
findings.impact: subprocess.run terminates batch_check only; in-flight fetch children continue consuming process/network resources after MCP reports timeout. The test uses the existing INN_CHECK_BATCH_ENGINE test seam, not an arbitrary-engine parameter exposed by MCP. Production impact depends on a timeout occurring; no indefinite runaway was demonstrated.
findings.fix: Start each tool run in its own process group/session and terminate/reap the entire descendant group on timeout (with a Windows equivalent), or implement explicit child cancellation in batch_check.
